Built and syntax-checked. Reload **http://maker:4001** and re-save the blocked link:

```
https://blocked.example/secret-report
```

Give it a title (e.g. "Secret report") and save. Now on its card in the list, check the two things you asked for:

1. **Clear "not preserved" notice** — the card shows: *"Page couldn't be read — details entered by you, and the page was not preserved (the image is a placeholder),"* so nothing implies the placeholder is a real saved copy.
2. **Retry** — click **"Retry now."** For this demo I simulate the page having become accessible: it then **reads the page, fills in the title/description if you left them blank, and replaces the placeholder** with the real icon/preview, and the notice disappears.

(Note: retrying the actual *preserved copy* of the page belongs with the preservation feature, which is a later cycle — I've recorded that; here the retry re-collects the page details.)

Does that distinction — "not preserved" vs. a real copy, plus retry — feel right? Once you confirm, I'll move to the last group of edge cases: **very long text and a large number of bookmarks.**
